h1:
Pattaya Food Guide
Seafood, Buffets, Cafes & Night Markets
intro: Pattaya is a town you can eat your way through from morning till late at night — fresh seafood by the water in Naklua, hotel buffets with bay views, clifftop cafes around Pratamnak, and night markets where you can graze for hours. We've rounded up what's worth eating, which neighborhoods to head for, and roughly what it costs, so you can plan your meals before you even set off.

blocks.html: Ask what to eat in Pattaya and the short answer is seafood — but the town has a lot more than that. There's local-priced seafood up in Naklua, hotel buffets where you can watch the sunset, photogenic sea-view cafes, and night markets where the food stalls run for what feels like a kilometre. We've split everything into categories and noted the neighborhood and price range, so you can pick by budget and the kind of trip you're after.

blocks.title: Read this first
blocks.html: Prices here are rough ranges from recent reviews. Seafood is charged by weight and season (crab and prawns move with the catch), and hotel buffets usually bump their rates over long weekends and high season. Check the price for your travel dates to be sure.

blocks.text: Pattaya seafood — where and which neighborhood to eat

blocks.html: Pattaya's real seafood neighborhood is Naklua, at the north end of town, especially around Lan Pho Market where the fishing boats come in. That means fresher catch at gentler prices than central Pattaya Beach. If you'd rather sit by the sand and take it slow, there are restaurants spread from Jomtien up to Naklua — pick the vibe you like.

items.name: Lan Pho Market, Naklua
items.blurb: A seaside market that's Pattaya's source for fresh seafood. Buy prawns, shellfish, crab and fish raw and have a stall cook them for you, or sit down at one of the seafood restaurants around the market. Friendlier prices than the central beach zone, with a genuine local-market feel.
items.meta: Naklua · open late morning to evening

items.name: Krua Talay Lan Pho Seafood
items.blurb: A Naklua seafood spot that locals pack out. The draw is fresh catch at prices that don't sting. Crowd favorites are curry-powder crab, grilled prawns, blanched cockles, and a late-night seafood rice soup.

items.name: Mum Aroi, Naklua
items.blurb: A waterfront spot that gets fresh ingredients thanks to being close to the fishing grounds. You eat while looking out over the sea — good for an unhurried, easygoing dinner.

items.name: Madame Hoi Seafood Sod
items.blurb: A seafood restaurant near Lan Pho Market with both an air-conditioned room and outdoor tables by the water. Good for groups or families — order set platters to share.

items.name: Beachfront seafood at Jomtien
items.blurb: The Jomtien strip has several seafood restaurants lined up along the beach, where you can dig your toes into the sand while you eat. Good for couples or small groups who want the beach atmosphere more than rock-bottom prices.

blocks.title: Getting your money's worth on seafood
blocks.html: Always ask the price per kilo and the actual weight before you order, especially for big crab and prawns — have the stall weigh it in front of you and do the rough maths before you agree. That way there are no surprises when the bill comes. For freshness, look for clear eyes, shiny shells, and no strong smell.

blocks.text: Pattaya buffets — beachfront hotels and seafood

blocks.html: Most Pattaya buffets are inside beachfront hotels, and the appeal is getting both variety and a view over Pattaya Bay. Prices depend on the day and the seating. Evening seafood spreads tend to cost more and only run on certain days, while regular international buffets are easier on the wallet. Book ahead on holidays — they fill up fast.

items.name: Edge — Hilton Pattaya
items.blurb: A 14th-floor restaurant with a panoramic view over Pattaya Bay, running a seafood buffet on select days. The highlights are oysters, prawns and sushi — a nice setting for a special meal or a celebration.
items.price: seafood buffet from around ฿999++ (varies by seating/day)

items.name: InterContinental Pattaya Resort
items.blurb: A seafood barbecue buffet on select days in a resort setting by the sea at Na Jomtien, with fresh seafood, grilled dishes, and premium options. Good for anyone after a fancier meal in a quieter atmosphere.
items.price: low four figures per head (check each week's promo)

items.name: Grand Centre Point Pattaya
items.blurb: An evening international buffet in a hotel in the middle of town, with Thai, Japanese and Western dishes. More affordable than a seafood buffet — good for families who want variety in one place.

items.name: Siam Design Hotel Pattaya
items.blurb: A good-value buffet in the center of town, with an unlimited-time evening seating and drinks included. Good for groups of friends or anyone on a tighter budget who still wants a hotel buffet.

blocks.title: Booking a buffet the smart way
blocks.html: Many hotel seafood buffets only run on certain days (often Saturdays), and the per-head price climbs on long weekends. Call or check the hotel's page before you go, and ask whether drinks and tax are included — the price you see advertised is sometimes before the ++ is added.

blocks.text: Pattaya cafes — sea views and photo spots

blocks.html: Pattaya's cafes split roughly into two zones. The Pratamnak and Naklua side is all about sea views and sunsets, while in town you'll find minimalist, photo-friendly cafes scattered around. If you like sitting out in the evening catching the sea breeze, the Pratamnak zone has the best atmosphere.

items.name: The Sky Gallery Pattaya
items.blurb: A cafe and restaurant on the Pratamnak hillside with a wide sea view — great for catching the evening breeze and taking photos. It gets busy around sunset, so arriving early or booking ahead pays off.

items.name: Treescape Pattaya
items.blurb: A leafy, shaded cafe and restaurant in the Pattaya–Naklua area with plenty of photo corners. Good for settling in for a while, whether for coffee or a full meal.

items.name: Beachfront cafes at Jomtien
items.blurb: The Jomtien zone has several cafes right by the sand, where you can sip coffee close to the water. Good for a daytime break before heading back to the evening markets.

blocks.text: Pattaya night markets and street food

blocks.html: Night-time eating is part of Pattaya's charm. The evening markets are made for grazing — lots of variety at prices from a few tens to a few hundred baht, perfect for an easy meal after a full day out. We've picked the markets with the best food and the most fun to wander.

items: Thepprasit Night Market — Pattaya's biggest night market, open roughly 5:00 pm to 11:00 pm, with food, clothes and souvenirs, plus parking and restrooms. Standout bites include grilled pork and chicken skewers, grilled seafood, shaved-ice desserts, and a few quirky dishes worth trying.
Lan Pho Market, Naklua (evening) — beyond buying fresh seafood, there are seaside snacks and sit-down stalls in the evening, with the feel of a local market by the water.
Evening markets around Central and South Pattaya — day markets and street-food stalls scattered through the side streets, easy to find near your hotel and handy for a late meal without going far.
Pattaya beachfront street food — carts and stalls along the seafront walkway, with fried snacks, grilled food, fruit and sweets you can pick at as you stroll.

blocks.title: Night out, stay sensible
blocks.html: Pattaya has nightlife districts like Walking Street. If you're going to wander, eat, and soak up the atmosphere, drink in moderation, keep an eye on your valuables and bag in the crowds, check prices before ordering drinks at some bars, and split your cash into separate stashes — it's just more reassuring.

blocks.text: Pattaya food by budget and style

items: Budget (฿100–300 per head) — wander Thepprasit Market for street food, or share local seafood dishes in Naklua.
Mid-range (฿300–700 per head) — beachfront seafood restaurants at Jomtien, or an international hotel buffet.
Splurge / special occasion (low four figures per head) — a seafood buffet at a beachfront hotel with a bay view, good for a celebration or a romantic meal.
Cafe and photo crowd — the Pratamnak and Naklua zones in the evening for sunset views.

faq.q: Where's the best place to eat seafood in Pattaya without paying a lot?
faq.a: The Naklua area, especially around Lan Pho Market, is the source for fresh, local-priced seafood because it's close to the fishing grounds. You can buy it fresh and have a stall cook it, or eat at the seafood restaurants around the market — both run cheaper than the central Pattaya Beach zone.

faq.q: Roughly how much does a Pattaya seafood buffet cost?
faq.a: Seafood buffets at beachfront hotels usually run in the low four figures per head and only happen on certain days. Regular international buffets start at around 750 baht per head. Prices often rise over long weekends, so book and check the rate for your dates first.

faq.q: What's the biggest night market in Pattaya?
faq.a: Thepprasit Night Market is Pattaya's biggest, open roughly 5:00 pm to 11:00 pm, with food, clothes and souvenirs plus parking and restrooms. It's ideal for a long graze after a full day out.

faq.q: Which zone has Pattaya's sea-view cafes?
faq.a: The Pratamnak and Naklua zones have the best sea views and sunsets — for example, The Sky Gallery up on the Pratamnak hillside. Jomtien also has cafes right by the beach where you can sit close to the water.

faq.q: What should I watch out for on a night out eating in Pattaya?
faq.a: Pattaya has nightlife districts, so be sensible: drink in moderation, watch your valuables and bag in the crowds, and check prices before ordering drinks at some bars to avoid a blown-up bill.
